fix: Either land the source continuation as the production path, with its constructor installed at node start, or stop loading it and remove the dead branches. Move the carry to the octet buffer (books/octets-stobj.lisp), with ACL2 resuming from a saved frame offset, as the served NNTP read already does.

reviewer: *fnn-tcl-source-start* defaults to nil (tcpcl.lisp:145), and git grep shows it bound only in tests/bp_segmented_wire_native_recording.lisp and tests/tcpcl_source_continuation_host_refuter-mock.lisp. The source-input branches (lines 325, 407-419, 531) are therefore test-only code shipped in the image. The live branch (lines 529-536) converts every read to an octet list (fnn-octet-list incoming) and calls fn-tcl-host-drive on (append carry chunk), keeping the returned carry. ACL2 re-frames from the start of the carry on every read, which is quadratic list work in the partial-segment size on a peer-driven path and the runtime octet-list representation D27 forbids.
scenario: In the image, the source-pending and source-more branches and fnn-tcl-source-input-turn can never run, but they are loaded and stay in the session loop. The path that does run conses every received byte into a list and appends each read to the retained carry, so ACL2 re-frames from the start of the carry on every read. A peer sending a segment of size S in reads of c octets costs O(S^2/c) list work and about 16 x S bytes of conses per partial segment. This is D27's runtime octet-list representation on a peer-driven BP path.
title: TCPCL: the received-source path is test-only code loaded in production, and the live path re-drives an ever-growing octet-list carry
